cards_resequenced.change: The job about supplier invoice numbers was written as though the system already stored the supplier's invoice number. It does not, and never has: there is no such box in the database. A second job on the list was written the same way, each assuming the other had already built it. This job now builds it, together with the letter code that goes in front of it, because a letter code with no number attached identifies nothing.

The job that separates the supplier's document number from our own now formally waits for the job above, since it cannot start until the supplier's number exists. It keeps our own number and nothing else changes about it.

The same job was also asked to prove its new checks fail before the fix and pass after, in two separate runs. That is impossible here: the overnight run's own safety checks reject the first of the two runs in under thirty seconds, before any test executes, and that is exactly what happened last night. The proof is now a permanent commit reference anybody can re-run at any time, which is stronger than a build log that expires.

The question waiting for you about the database integration overstated its own danger. It says a merged deletion could wipe production data. It cannot: the guard it asked for was built four days ago and runs on every change. The question is still yours to answer and still waiting, it is just smaller than it looked.

The job about the credential lockdown checklist now records a third gap in the same family: the lockdown removes the permission that forty-five unfinished jobs need in order to finish themselves, and it lists only one job as coming before it.

escalations.title: Two settings in the hosting console are the only things left between the low-stock warning emails and working for real, and they have not moved since 31 August. Nobody but you can set them.
escalations.recommendation: Set both in the production environment in one sitting: the email service key, and the address the warnings are sent from. Ten minutes. RECOMMENDED BECAUSE THE REST IS ALREADY BUILT AND PROVEN: the warning logic passes four automated tests, so these two settings are the whole remaining gap on our side. THE HONEST CAVEAT, WHICH HAS BEEN STATED EVERY TIME AND IS STATED AGAIN: setting them does not finish this on its own. The system currently addresses the warning to an account on a domain that does not exist, and that address is replaced when the real client accounts are created at the handover job. So this is one of three things, not the last one. IF UNANSWERED: nothing breaks. Stock can fall below its threshold on the live site and no email is sent, silently, and the screen shows the warning as unsent. That has been the state for eleven days and will continue until you set them.
